- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-day moving average.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.0 to -0.5 within 3 days), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean price; apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is flat (0.1–0.3) and price is trending, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 30-day high, model tends to overreact; apply 1–2% downward correction to avoid overbought bias.
